hints: Focus on how the oxygen already inside the molecule reduces the oxygen needed from the air for complete combustion.

Write out the molecular formula for each 3-carbon compound, propane is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$, propan-1-ol is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$, propanone is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$ and propanoic acid is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$.
Balance $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O} + x\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$ for oxygen atoms to find x, then check which other option gives that same 4.5 value.
walkthrough:
**Write the rule for complete combustion**

Think of combustion as adding oxygen until all C becomes $\text{CO}_2$ and all H becomes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Any O already in the fuel means you need less $\text{O}_2$ from the air.

General form:
$$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y\text{O}_z + \left(x + \frac{y}{4} - \frac{z}{2}\right)\text{O}_2 \rightarrow x\text{CO}_2 + \frac{y}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**List the molecular formulae**

All have 3 carbons, but different H and O counts. This is the key difference.

$$\text{propane: C}_3\text{H}_8$$
$$\text{propanoic acid: C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$$
$$\text{propanone: C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$$
$$\text{propan-1-ol: C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$$

**Calculate oxygen needed for propan-1-ol**

Balance C first, then H, then O. You get 3 $\text{CO}_2$ and 4 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ as products.

$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O} + 4.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Check O atoms: left has $1 + 9 = 10$, right has $6 + 4 = 10$. It balances perfectly, so 4.5 molecules of $\text{O}_2$ are required.

**Conclude the match**

Propane needs 5 $\text{O}_2$, propanone needs 4 $\text{O}_2$, and propanoic acid needs only 3.5 $\text{O}_2$ because it already contains two O atoms. Only propan-1-ol fits the 4.5 requirement.

options.A: Propane is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$ with no oxygen in it, so it needs the most external oxygen. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8 + 5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$, which is 5 not 4.5.
options.B: Propanoic acid is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$. It already contains two O atoms, so needs much less $\text{O}_2$. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2 + 3.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$, which is 3.5 not 4.5.
options.C: Propanone is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$. It needs $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O} + 4\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$, which is 4 not 4.5. Students often confuse it with the alcohol because both have one O, but the H count is different.
options.D: Propan-1-ol is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$. Complete combustion gives $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O} + 4.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Oxygen balances (10 on each side), so this exactly matches the 4.5 molecules required.
